## Summary

The change rejects owner creation with **400 Bad Request** when the email domain is on the disposable-domain blocklist.

I edited `OwnerRestControllerV1.normalizeEmail(...)` in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

- Added a `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` set (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`).
- After lower-casing and syntactic validation, the domain (the part after `@`) is checked against the blocklist; a match returns `false`, which the existing `addOwner`/`updateOwner` flow already translates into a `400 BAD_REQUEST`.

This fits the existing pattern: `normalizeEmail` was already the single gate for email validity returning 400, so blocklisted domains are handled consistently on both create and update. The case-insensitive match is guaranteed because the domain is compared after lower-casing.

Tests: `AcceptanceTest.errorRejectsDisposableDomain` (posts `x@mailinator.com`, expects 400) passes, and the full `mvnw test` build is green.
